approaches.objective: Upgrade directional occupation control to trace scale for all balanced cuts, producing the tight-prefix absorptive trace estimate with every source and damping term matched to the scalar Riccati bound.
Propagate the perimeter excess with a global operator-norm covariance weight at the unit-rate scale.
Charge the weighted excess only on the aligned screen where the trace term dominates, and return at most an absorbable fraction on its complement.
Specify the tensor-stable replacement for the refuted weighted package and supply the matching localization-uniform almost-stability trace theorem modulo Jacobi zero modes.
Define one bridge object carrying both the cut-free covariance index and the cut-indexed boundary geometry, and prove the covariance-taming or almost-splitting estimate from it.
Decide the incident-high product-cut model with a uniform analytic bound for fixed balanced product cuts, or a certified counterexample.
Prove the universal-time full-damping source estimate uniformly on regular approximants, preserving tensor orientation under unwhitening.
Close the occupation estimate on the published polylogarithmic covariance window through the initial-layer window chain.
Construct, for every centered log-concave law, one regular compact-target moment-map recovery sequence with a universal bound on the CMH liminf.

Prove the anisotropic source-retention inequality that would bound the linear-test quotient through the exact isotropic-coordinate matrices, working from the weak column equation of the linear-sector gate-matrix spectral resolution without assuming its strong operator-domain form, and supplying the integrated corrector or nonlocal coercivity that matrix polarization alone cannot.
Bound the CMH constant uniformly along the certified regular approximant families, a stronger premise than the recovery envelope and not needed if that one is discharged.
Derive the target-flat multiplier invariantly and reduce arbitrary split dimensions to controlled Codazzi components paired with named positive squares.
Control the complete Haar sum of square-root commutators on a common core, accounting for every retained positive and error term without double spending.

Compute the exact second variation through the Hodge split at an admissible target-side perturbation of the saturating one-sided-exponential product, aimed at the radial Gamma factor rather than at the base of an exponential cone.

Decide the necessary linear moment-map inequality, first in the sharp form of gate zero and then at the CMH constant itself, by an independently checked analytic argument or a genuine moment-map counterexample, using the certified third-moment decomposition of the linear sector and the exact exponential-cone battery as the equality set any argument must be tight on.
Construct one test-independent isotropic frame with a universal L2 gap on the maximal closed form domain.

Refute the all-frame gate with an exact uniform-simplex dual certificate of polynomial degree at least three whose objective tends to zero, the certified degree-two floors of the root-frame degree-two pencil identity having ruled out every degree-two refuter.
Establish a universal tangential Poincare gap for normalized cone measure, feeding the published Hardy boundary bridge.
Decide the rotation-optimized simplex transmission bound before registering a Laplace-Brenier route.
